ticket.title: miter deps tier 2: extraction simulation, layering fitness, dependency budgets and drift since a ref
ticket.description: Tier 2 of miter deps: the flags that turn the audit verdicts into measurements. (1) --what-if <crate::module|path> simulates an extraction from live data - who uses the module and from how many crates, which dependencies those consumers would stop pulling, and whether a cycle would appear - filling in the three-part extract test automatically. Naming: --what-if is primary with --simulate-extract as a visible alias; --extract was rejected because it reads as mutation, deps is read-only, and miter slice already owns how to extract. (2) --layers [--check] reads ordered layers from workspace.metadata.gaugeblock.layers and fails on upward edges - the architectural fitness function that turns crate strategy into a gate. (3) --budget [--max-crates N] fails when a consumer transitive tree grows, so adding regex to a core crate is caught in review. (4) --since <git-ref> reports new crate edges since a tag, making architectural drift visible per release. Depends on GB-161.
